candidates.name: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe
candidates.price: Adult €10, reduced €7, children under 18 years free, family €17
candidates.content: The museum is a leading centre for art, applied art, and design. Its collections of work from Europe and the Middle and the Far East are of the finest-quality and span all epochs from the Ancient World to the present day. They als

candidates.sec: The five main churches of Hamburg
candidates.name: Hauptkirche St. Nikolai
candidates.price: The price to take the elevator is €5 for adults and €4 for groups of at least 10 people
candidates.content: All five main churches of Hamburg were damaged in World War II. But in contrast to the other four, St. Nikolai has not been re-erected making it a memorial against war. It was designed by English architect George Gilbert Scott. Th

candidates.name: Internationales Maritimes Museum
candidates.content: This private museum in near the Speicherstadt district houses Peter Tamm's collection of model ships, construction plans, uniforms, and maritime art,. It opened in 2008 in the refurbished Kaispeicher B (quay warehouse B), which is

candidates.name: Cap San Diego
candidates.content: One of the last generation of pre-containerisation cargo ships (built in the 1960s), now semi-permanently moored halfway between Landungsbrücken and the Speicherstadt, and is the largest functional cargo museum ship in the world.

candidates.name: Museumshafen Oevelgönne
candidates.content: Historical boats.

candidates.name: Jenisch park
candidates.content: The oldest landscaped park in Hamburg. Two museums, Jenisch House and Ernst Barlach House, are in the park. Flottbek River flows through the park and into the Elbe at Teufelsbrück.

candidates.name: St.-Marien-Dom St. Georg
candidates.content: Since 1995, this neo-romanesque church is the cathedral of the youngest Roman Catholic archbishop of Germany. Though the church has not the splendor one might expect, next to it you may find the first statue world wide of the late

candidates.name: Bergedorf Castle
candidates.content: This is the only preserved castle inside the city borders of Hamburg, and it has been mentioned in documents in the 14th century. Since 1953 it houses a museum of Bergedorf and the Vierlande region. The idyllic castle park has bee

candidates.name: Petri und Pauli Kirche
candidates.content: A Lutheran church, and together with the castle the most important historical building in Bergedorf. The first church was built here in 1162, the current one was opened in 1502.

candidates.name: Kirche St. Michael
candidates.content: Built in 1955 in the form of a white cube extended in the east by the altar room, in the north by the sacristy and in the west by the lobby. The church is in the middle of the old graveyard.

candidates.name: Rieck Haus - Vierländer Freilichtmuseum
candidates.content: Open-air museum showcasing the rural life in the Vierlanden before the industrial revolution. The premises was an active farm operated by the Rieck family up until WWII. There are still farm animals there, and several hands-on exp

candidates.name: Kirche St. Johannis
candidates.content: After an earlier church, presumably made of rocks, was destroyed by flooding, this timber-framed one was built in 1599-1603. It is an open church and as such can generally be visited anytime (during daytime).

candidates.sec: The five main churches of Hamburg
candidates.name: Hauptkirche St. Michaelis
candidates.content: The youngest and most famous of the five is also the only baroque church. This building is not the original St. Michaelis - that one (built 1647-1669) was destroyed by a lightning strike in 1750. It was not until 1786 that the pre

candidates.sec: The five main churches of Hamburg
candidates.name: Hauptkirche St. Jacobi
candidates.content: St. Jacobi has been a parish since the 12th century, when it was not even within Hamburg's then city walls. The present-day church is a reconstruction of the late medieval one from the 15th century, which was destroyed during the

candidates.sec: The five main churches of Hamburg
candidates.name: Hauptkirche St. Petri
candidates.content: St. Petri was a cathedral as early as the 12th century or possibly even earlier. As with other Hauptkirchen, the present version is one of many successive, and was only completed in 1878 after the great fire in 1842 consumed its p

candidates.sec: The five main churches of Hamburg
candidates.name: Hauptkirche St. Katharinen
candidates.content: Situated on an island, it traditionally served as the church of the seamen. The base of its spire, dating from the 13th century, is the second oldest building preserved in the city. The church is also famous for its centuries-old

candidates.name: Altonaer Museum
candidates.content: Dedicated to Altona's, Hamburg's and northern Germany's cultural history.

candidates.name: Christianskirche
candidates.content: Baroque church in Ottensen.

candidates.name: Loki Schmidt Garten
candidates.hours: Daily open from 09:00 to about 1 hour before sunset
candidates.content: For a century and a half, the botanical garden was situated in the current Planten un Blomen park, where the tropical greenhouses still remain. In 1979, the botanical garden was relocated to its current place in the Klein Flottbek

candidates.name: Dreieinigkeitskirche St. Georg
candidates.content: Baroque church in Sankt Georg.

candidates.name: Franz-von-Assisi-Kirche
candidates.content: One of the newest churches in the region, this Lutheran church was inaugurated in 1993. The 40-m-high church tower is visible from far away.

candidates.name: Edith-Stein-Kirche
candidates.content: A modern Catholic church building inaugurated in 1993. It is a round church with a flat roof rising up towards the altar.

candidates.name: Kirche St. Severini
candidates.content: The biggest church in the Vierlande region. First built as a stone church in 1319, and thoroughly renovated in the late 18th century.

candidates.name: Kirche St. Nicolai
candidates.content: First mentioned in documents from 1247, this is the oldest of the village churches in the Vierlande.

candidates.name: St. Pankratius
candidates.content: This 17th-century church features carvings depicting scenes from the Old and New Testaments, and an organ by the famous organ builder Arp Schnitger.

candidates.name: The Hamburg Dungeon
candidates.content: A live-action presentation of the "darker times" of Hamburg. It is probably mostly suited for a younger, easily impressed audience. But it might not be suitable for young children.

candidates.name: Elbphilharmonie
candidates.content: New 'architectural lighthouse' of Hamburg. On the top of a huge old warehouse a 110 metres tall modern philharmonic hall with glass façade and wave-shaped roof. It also includes a fancy hotel, restaurant, as well as private apartm

candidates.name: Tierpark Hagenbeck
candidates.price: Adults: €20, children 4–16 years: €15, family: €60-70, with Tropen-Aquarium: €30, children: , family: €85-98
candidates.content: Hamburg's Zoo. The collection began in 1863 with animals that belonged to Carl Hagenbeck Sr. (1810–1887), a fishmonger who became an amateur animal collector. The park itself was founded by Carl Hagenbeck Jr. in 1907. It is known

candidates.name: Hamburger SV
candidates.content: Die Rothosen (The Red Shorts) were promoted in 2025 and play soccer in Bundesliga, the top tier. Volksparkstadion has a capacity of 57,000 for domestic games and 51,500 for internationals and occasionally hosts concerts. In 2024 i

candidates.name: FC St Pauli
candidates.content: The Kiezkicker ("Neighbourhood Kickers") were relegated in 2026 and now play soccer in 2. Bundesliga, the second tier. Millerntor-Stadion has a capacity of 29,500 and is also used for concerts.

candidates.name: Hamburgische Staatsoper
candidates.content: Hamburg is home to the Hamburg State Opera House, one of the leading opera houses in Germany. It holds great historical significance, as in 1678 the first public opera house in Germany was built in Hamburg at Gänsemarkt Square, wh

candidates.name: Laeiszhalle
candidates.content: The Laeiszhalle is the main classical music hall in Hamburg, with two halls: the kleiner Saal and großer Saal. You can see the schedule on their website. For online ticket purchases, use Ticket Online.

candidates.name: Thalia Theater
candidates.content: New directors and the continuing cooperation with young important writers based on the confidence in a strong and vital company lead to international acknowledgment.

candidates.name: Ernst-Deutsch-Theater
candidates.content: The Ernst-Deutsch-Theater has been an established part of the Hamburg theatre scene since 1951. Today, it is the largest privately operated playhouse in Germany.

candidates.name: Kirschblütenfest
candidates.content: On May 19, the Japanese community of Hamburg celebrates the Japanese Cherry Blossom Festival by the Lake Alster. Enormous fireworks and a peaceful atmosphere are characteristics of this event.

candidates.name: Hamburger Dom
candidates.content: The Dom is one of the largest fairs in Germany. The streets of the fairground, lined on both sides with rides, amusements and food and drink stalls, are some 3.3 km long. It takes place for three separate months in spring, su

candidates.name: Schmidt Theater
candidates.content: Schmidt Theater is a private theater at Spielbudenplatz. It consists of two venues, the Schmidt Theater itself and the Schmidts Tivoli (also known as Grosses Haus), which is just a stone's throw away.

candidates.name: Hamburg Planetarium
candidates.content: Features multiple visual shows a day, and an observation deck.

candidates.name: St. Pauli Theater
candidates.content: It opened in 1841 as the Urania Theater and took its present name in 1941.

candidates.name: Hafenrundfahrten
candidates.content: From Landungsbrücken, you can make boat tours into the harbour, available from various companies and take around an hour. Big ships provide more comfort, but smaller ships also go through the Speicherstadt. Both are well worth the

candidates.name: HADAG Ferries
candidates.content: A low-budget alternative for a boat tour on the river Elbe. A part of Hamburg's public transport system (HVV). If you have already bought a HVV day ticket, the ride is free. Most tourists take ferry 62 from Landungsbrücken to Fink

candidates.name: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe
candidates.content: The Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe Hamburg has many smaller concerts — something almost every day — and is much cheaper than the Laeiszhalle. The programs range from the curator of their early keyboard instrument collection playing

candidates.name: The Rover Rep Theatre
candidates.content: At the Irish Rover. English language pub theatre under the Irish Rover at the Großneumarkt. High class professional productions in a special atmosphere.

candidates.name: The English Theatre of Hamburg
candidates.content: The English Theatre of Hamburg performs from September through June, giving eight performances per week.

candidates.name: The Hamburg Players
candidates.content: Hamburg's oldest English-language theatre group giving three shows a year at the Theater in der Marschnerstraße.

candidates.name: Supper Club
candidates.content: Supper Club's name doesn't give you any clues about this business. It hires canoes and all manner of other unpowered water craft by the hour. When you have finished paddling you can eat at the outdoor cafe if you wish. A 2 hour pa

candidates.name: Theater im Hafen Hamburg
candidates.content: Watch The Lion King here. For many Germans this is the must-do when visiting Hamburg.

candidates.name: Stage Theater an der Elbe
candidates.content: Another musical venue. Mary Poppins is showing here until Aug 2019, then Pretty Woman will take the stage in Sep 2019.

candidates.name: Molotow/Top Ten Bar
candidates.content: Concert location and club.

candidates.name: Headcrash
candidates.content: Concert location and club.

candidates.name: Uebel und Gefährlich
candidates.content: In a former bunker from World War II, it can be found near St. Pauli in Feldstraße. Easy to reach with the metro U3. Music used to be more hard house and electro but is changing nowadays from day to day.

candidates.name: Tunnel
candidates.content: If you are more into Trance, Techno and Schranz the Tunnel might be a good place.

candidates.name: BPSchanzen1
candidates.content: A tiny bar that houses many different DJs. The atmosphere is very friendly and good music is played. It's opposite the house that is occupied by various leftist fractions. (The yellow building with all the graffiti, named 'rote Fl

candidates.name: Gun Club
candidates.content: Grungy but friendly punk bar in a cellar just off the Davidstraße. Came second in Hamburg Mexikanercontest (Mexikaner is a shot drink very similar to a bloody mary), and it shows - definitely the recommended drink here.

candidates.name: Komet
candidates.content: 1950s, 60s and 70s rock, soul, R&B and similar in an entirely appropriate setting with cinema couches, pulp film posters and a (rather decrepit) Wurlitzer.

candidates.name: Eldorado
candidates.content: 1960s and 1970s music in entirely period setting, with wallpaper and ceiling that seem to be completely original and at least 40 years old, and furniture to match.

candidates.name: Shebeen
candidates.content: Cheap & cheerful bar with minimalist decoration celebrating St.Pauli FC and other friendly clubs. It's a hangout of the St.Pauli Ultras. Outsiders very welcome, but if you don't agree with what St.Pauli stands for, this is not the

candidates.name: Washington-Bar
candidates.content: Relaxed bar covered in Hunter S. Thompson quotes with atmosphere to match. Small dance floor with DJ who plays everything from psychedelic jazz to German hip-hop. Excellent selection of gin&tonics.

candidates.name: Zur Ritze
candidates.content: Zur Ritze is fairly easy to find. It's near the Beatlesplatz at Reeperbahn; follow the signage down a small alley to the almost legendary door. The bar is almost always open, and it's a beautiful place to sit and talk all night. H

candidates.name: Pampa
candidates.content: The outdoor bars and cafes of Karolinenviertel merge with those of the southern part of the Schanzenviertel neighbourhood making one of Europe's great outdoor dining areas (at least in Summer). Pampa Bar is a great example. Plenty

candidates.name: Brauhaus Joh. Albrecht
candidates.content: Cosy brewpub with good beers and food.

candidates.name: St. Pauli Fischmarkt
candidates.content: For Germans, it's a classic to eat bread with fish on St. Pauli Fischmarkt, especially very early in the Sunday morning (meaning 05:00 - 09:30) when visiting Hamburg. If for breakfast or as an after-party snack may depend on your

candidates.name: Lühmanns Teestube
candidates.content: Friendly local café. Light fare and local specialties, wonderful pies, and baked goods. Their Cornish tea with fresh scones is worth trying.

candidates.name: Ristorante Borsalino
candidates.content: Sternstraße 125, three minutes from S-Bahn station Sternschanze in the trendy neighbourhood of Schanzenviertel. Pizzas start from €6, fresh pasta is around €7-10 (try Pasta Mista), the meat dishes are delicious (it is right next t

candidates.name: Kombüse
candidates.content: Mexican meets Hamburg punk/alternative. Excellent fresh ingredients. Vegan & veggie options (but also meat for the carnivores), with a huge range of hot sauces. Prices are low (€10.50 or less as of April 2015) and portions are hug

candidates.name: McBoat
candidates.hours: Open 24 hours but closed in winter
candidates.content: The only McDonald's that you can order your meal (on its app) and have it delivered to the shores while paddling along the canal. The meal is prepared fresh in the restaurant right next to the shoreline.

candidates.name: Restaurant Cox
candidates.price: Dinner including wine is approximately €30-40. They have a value lunch deal (two course menu for €11)
candidates.content: Trendy restaurant with consistently good international cuisine, often local German dishes

candidates.name: Cafe Paris
candidates.content: Classic French bistro in a beautiful historical building. Good place to get a coffee and pastry, or enjoy a leisurely lunch. Ground floor is very loud, crowded and busy. Upstairs (when entering turn right) is a quiet restaurant wi

candidates.name: Der Etrusker
candidates.content: Small and quite crowded Italian restaurant in the "Grindel" district near the university. Excellent Italian classics (pizza, pasta, etc.) for reasonable money. A lot of Italian restaurants as alternative to the left and right if y

candidates.name: La Monella
candidates.content: Hamburg's first vegetarian Italian restaurant. Small menu with Italian standards. Daily menu with dishes made of regional ingredients. Good place for a very delicious vegetarian lunch on a budget. Dinner slightly overpriced.

candidates.name: Restaurant Kalliopea
candidates.content: Traditional Greek food.

candidates.name: Joker
candidates.content: Great for a quick bite before going out in the area. Try the Oriental Chicken!

candidates.name: Feldstern
candidates.content: Cozy pub/restaurant with affordable German food and outside seating in the summer. Nice lunch menu from 12:00-16:00 on weekdays.

candidates.name: Isemarkt
candidates.content: Europe's longest open market, under the U3 subway driveway between Hoheluftbrücke and Eppendorfer Baum between the two lanes of the Isestraße.

december.text: Wall-Anlagen: The western part of the former city wall is nowadays a park area surrounding the inner city as a semicircle, ranging from the Landungsbrücken (Helgoländer Allee) up to Binnenalster.
